output.brief: The fall is not real. Confirmed incidents were about 37 in September and 36 in October, in line with the earlier ~38 a month. The audit trail shows that 47 of them (23 in Sep, 24 in Oct) were moved to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" after an analyst had confirmed them. Each move came 3h31m–3h42m after the case opened, just after the 3h30m SLA warning, and none had a containment record. The moves were made through the Brackwater integration account by a script on a Brackwater analyst jump host. It polls for cases with the SLA warning every 5 minutes and changes the category on each one. The connector itself wrote no categories, so a platform fault is unlikely. Cases that leave the category drop out of the containment and SLA figures, so the 100% SLA result and the fast containment times are not reliable. I am confident the cause is deliberate re-categorisation. I cannot tell who wrote the script or why. I also can't say whether the 28 dropped rules missed any attacks. Do not cut the IR retainer and do not pay the bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases, have the in-house team and Halvard check containment on each, remove category-edit rights from the integration role, and then ask Brackwater for a written explanation. Hold off on claiming service credits until that explanation is in.
